summary: The installed system compiling a C program on itself with tcc, refusing the output kinds it cannot run with their reasons, building this project's own programs, and asking the kernel for no system call it lacks

cases.behavior: The installed system, as the test account at the console, compiles a C program with tcc and runs it; refuses -run, -shared, a link without -static and a raw-image link, each with its reason and with no output left; compiles an object; builds this project's cat, which agrees with BusyBox's over a 21 KB binary file and over two files; links ping from two sources; runs a program in which the x86-64 compiler must clear the high half of an unsigned int it converts to floating point, and scale a negative index and a row of 2 GiB of an array of variable length in the pointer's width; runs a program whose array parameters are sized by earlier parameters, and one whose bounds have side effects, earlier bindings, inner constants and an old-style declaration list, and one whose bound reads a volatile object on entry, and one whose bounds and statements throw away volatile reads that must still be made, and gets GCC's results; refuses [*] in a definition; runs a static program calling an IFUNC its assembler defines and gets GCC's result; and the kernel's trace of missing system calls names none that tcc asked for

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the disk copy and its evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot a copy of the os-real disk with the trace of missing system calls on, and log in at the console as the test account
write /tmp/hello.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it
ask tcc for -run, -shared, a link without -static and a raw-image link, printing each status and what tcc said, and look for their outputs
compile /tmp/hello.c to an object with tcc -c
compile /src/utils/cat.c, and compare it with BusyBox's cat over 21 KB of /bin/tcc and over two files
link ping from /src/utils/ping.c and /src/utils/resolv.c in one command
write /tmp/wide.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it
write /tmp/vparm.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it

write /tmp/vbound.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it, write /tmp/vread.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it, write /tmp/vdisc.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it, and compile a definition with int a[*] with tcc -c, printing its status and what tcc said
write /tmp/ifunc.c with printf, compile it with tcc -static and run it
sync, end the machine with QMP's quit, and read the trace on the whole console

assertions.checks: the test account logs in at the console with its password and reaches the shell's prompt
tcc -static builds /tmp/hello from /tmp/hello.c
the program the machine compiled runs and prints COMPILEDHERE
tcc -run exits with status 1
tcc -run says that code it runs from memory cannot reach the C library
tcc -shared exits with status 1
tcc -shared says that -shared is not available
a link without -static exits with status 1
a link without -static says that a program must be linked with -static
a link with -Wl,-oformat=binary exits with status 1
a link with -Wl,-oformat=binary says that a program must be an ELF
none of the four refused compiles left its output file, which the guest checks
tcc -c makes an object, which is not refused
tcc -static builds this project's cat from /src/utils/cat.c
the 21 KB input of the comparison is made from /bin/tcc
the cat the machine built writes the same bytes as BusyBox's cat over the 21 KB input, which cmp in the guest judges
the cat the machine built writes the same bytes as BusyBox's cat over two files, which cmp in the guest judges
tcc -static links ping from two sources in one command
tcc -static builds /tmp/wide from /tmp/wide.c

the program prints WIDENED 1 1 1 12 2147483648 on x86-64: an unsigned int cast from 0x100000001 in a register converts to 1 as a double, a float and a long double, a pointer to the last row of int[3][3] less one points 12 bytes into the array, and a pointer to a row of 0x80000000 chars plus one moves forward 2147483648 bytes in a mapping of that size; on i686, where musl's mmap refuses a length of 0x80000000, it prints WIDENED 1 1 1 12 0
tcc -static builds /tmp/vparm from /tmp/vparm.c, whose functions take int a[n], int a[n][m] and, in a prototype, int a[*]

the program prints VLAPARAM 46 3612 40, as GCC's does: f(4, x) sums int a[n] after h, declared with int a[*] and defined with int a[n], set x[3] to 40; g(2, 3, y) weights the rows of int a[n][m] to 36 and adds sizeof a[0], 12; and x[3] is 40
tcc -static builds /tmp/vbound from /tmp/vbound.c, whose functions take int a[(k++,3)], int a[][n] before the parameter n, int a[][3][k], and int a[k][m] in an old-style declaration list

the program prints VLABOUNDS 6 1207 48 9 1205, as GCC's does: f(5, x) returns k incremented by its bound (k++,3) on entry; g(y, 7) gives sizeof a[0] of the global n's 3 ints, 12, and the parameter n; t(4, z) gives sizeof a[0] of int[3][4], 48, and stores 9 in z[1][2][3]; and r(2, 3, y) gives sizeof a[0], 12, and y[1][2], 5
tcc -static builds /tmp/vread from /tmp/vread.c, whose function takes int a[(*vp+1,3)] with vp a null pointer to a volatile int
the program prints VOLATILEREAD, as GCC's does: the bound (*vp+1,3) folds to 3 but reads *vp on entry to the function, and the read of address 0 reaches the program's SIGSEGV handler

tcc -static builds /tmp/vdisc from /tmp/vdisc.c, whose functions take int a[((int)*vp,3)], int a[((void)*vp,3)] and int a[(*vp,3)] and run (void)*vp;, *vp; and (int)*vp; with vp a null pointer to a volatile int

the program prints VDISCARD 111111, as GCC's does: each of the three bounds on entry and each of the three statements reads *vp although its value is thrown away, and each read of address 0 reaches the program's SIGSEGV handler, which jumps back for the next case
tcc -c of void q(int a[*]){} exits with status 1
tcc says '[*]' not allowed for the definition with int a[*]
tcc -static builds /tmp/ifunc from /tmp/ifunc.c, whose assembly defines pick with .type pick,@gnu_indirect_function as a resolver returning triple

the program prints IFUNCCALL 21 15 6 1, as GCC's does: pick(7), a pointer to pick taken at run time called with 5 and one in initialized data called with 2 each reach triple, and the two pointers are equal
sync returns and the shell comes back after the last line
no line of the kernel's trace on the whole console says that a call tcc asked for is not implemented

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case boots the installed system with rach2.trace=enosys on the kernel's command line, whose records of missing system calls judge the compiler
